_strings.@@fcab89219412: Treaty conformity — IA conforms to federal treaty treatment — income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is also excluded from IA income (it flows through the federal starting point; do not add it back on the IA return). (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state can conform on treaties while DECOUPLING from the federal Code for deductions or credits; see any law-change lines below.) State note: Iowa conforms. The 2025 IA 1040 keeps the redesign's starting point — "federal taxable income" — with Step 4 computing Iowa taxable income as federal taxable income (IA 1040 line 2, from federal 1040 line 15) plus net Iowa modifications from IA 1040 Schedule 1 (line 3, from Schedule 1 line 21). Lines 1a-1f (federal total income, adjustments, AGI, standard/itemized deduction, QBI deduction, and — new for 2025 — the federal senior deduction) are printed for reference only ("Do not include lines 1a through 1f"). Iowa applies rolling IRC conformity. Federally treaty-exempt income is excluded from federal AGI/federal taxable income before it ever reaches the Iowa return, and there is NO treaty/foreign-income re-inclusion among the Schedule 1 Column A additions. Reinforced by Iowa Admin. Code rule 701—300.17 (a resident is taxed on all income "except when an item of income is specifically exempted from taxation by a provision of federal or Iowa law"). Therefore treaty-exempt income is not re-taxed.
_strings.@@fd4d92a7a276: Low-Income Exemption (with elevated threshold for filers age 65+) — An exemption from Iowa income tax (not a dollar credit) functioning as Iowa's primary low-income and senior relief. A taxpayer is exempt from Iowa income tax if Iowa taxable income (IA 1040 line 4, with required add-backs) is at or below the threshold for their filing status. NEW for 2025 — the federal 'Enhanced Deduction for Seniors' is treated as a personal exemption that must be ADDED BACK when calculating the low-income exemption.

state_tax.work_common_tail: . Exemption-credit rules (IA 1040): Step 3a (personal): Step 3 line a. Expanded Instructions, Exemption Credits: "If you are filing single (status 1), married filing separately (status 3) or qualifying surviving spouse (status 5), enter 1 in the Personal Credit space. If you are filing married filing jointly (status 2) or head of household (status 4), you are eligible for an extra credit and should enter 2 in the Personal Credit space. Add the number of personal credits and multiply by $40." "Note to dependents filing their own returns: You may claim a $40 personal exemption credit even if you are claimed as a dependent on another person's Iowa return." Head of household enters 2 in Iowa. Step 3b (senior): The 65-or-older boxes of Step 3 line b. Expanded Instructions: "If you were 65 or older on or before January 1, 2026, you may take an additional personal credit. If your spouse was 65 or older on or before January 1, 2026, and you are filing a joint return (status 2), you may take an additional personal credit for your spouse." Line b is one count on the form: enter senior + blind there. A qualifying surviving spouse (status 5) files no joint return, so it counts the filer alone. Step 3b (blind): The blind boxes of Step 3 line b. Expanded Instructions: "If you were blind on December 31, 2025, you may take an additional personal credit. If your spouse was blind on December 31, 2025, and you are filing a joint return (status 2), you may take an additional personal credit for your spouse. Add the number of credits for 65 or older and blind and multiply by $20." Step 3c (dependent): Step 3 line c. Expanded Instructions: "Enter the number of dependent children and other dependents you are claiming for federal income tax purposes. Add the number of dependent credits and multiply by $40." "Married Separate Filers: You must report the same dependents you claimed on your federal income tax return." Expanded Instructions, Exemption Credits: "d. Total Add the dollar amounts and enter on Step 3, line d and on line 8." Line 08: "Enter the total exemption credit amount from IA 1040, Step 3, line d." No AGI limitation: the 2025 face and Expanded Instructions print none for Step 3. Line 12 here is counted from the op's tax (line 5): line 7 "Total tax. Add lines 5 and 6" adds the line 6 lump-sum tax, and line 11 adds the line 9 tuition/textbook and line 10 volunteer credits to line 8. It equals the filed line 12 when lines 6, 9 and 10 are zero; otherwise add those on the form. The alternate tax, tax reduction worksheet and low-income exemption change line 5 or 12 on the form (see the pack notes). This op computes the state's flat-rate tax line and, when exemption_credit_counts is passed, its exemption credits ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, other state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: 2025 STRUCTURAL CHANGE (SF 2442, enacted May 2024): Iowa went FLAT. The three 2024 brackets (4.40%/4.82%/5.70%) are GONE — for tax years beginning on or after 1/1/2025 there is a SINGLE flat rate of 3.8% on Iowa taxable income (IA 1040 line 5 = line 4 x 3.8%). Do NOT apply 2024 bracket figures to 2025, and do NOT use this pack for 2024. Base guidance: supply 2025 IA 1040 line 4 'Iowa taxable income' = line 2 federal taxable income (federal 1040, line 15) + line 3 net Iowa modifications (IA 1040 Schedule 1, line 21). Lines 1a-1f (federal total income, adjustments, AGI, standard/itemized deduction, QBI deduction, and — new for 2025 — the federal senior deduction) are printed for reference only. The federal standard/itemized and QBI deductions are already inside federal taxable income — Iowa has no state standard deduction or base personal exemptions, so this op subtracts nothing before applying the 3.8% rate (standard_deduction is null; exemptions is empty). Flat rate makes filing status irrelevant to line 5: with a single 3.8% rate and no per-status standard deduction, single / MFS / HoH / MFJ all compute the identical tax on the same base. The op's qualifying-surviving-spouse -> married_filing_jointly aliasing (which was a CRITICAL understatement warning in the 2024 graduated pack, since Iowa status 5 is NON-JOINT on the bracket worksheet) is now HARMLESS — the flat rate is status-independent. It matters only for the ALTERNATE tax (off-model, below). Alternate tax (NOT modeled) survives for 2025 at a REDUCED rate: all statuses except single may compute an alternate tax on the 2025 IA 1040 Alternate Tax Worksheet (41-145) — 4.3% (.043), DOWN from 5.7% in 2024 — of income above $13,500 ($32,000 if you or your spouse was 65 or older on 12/31/2025), and enter the SMALLER of that or 3.8% x line 4 on line 5 (check the Step 5 box). Status-3 (MFS) spouses prorate it. This provision is REPEALED for tax years beginning on or after 1/1/2026. Single taxpayers may instead qualify for the Iowa Income Tax Reduction Worksheet (41-146). Check these when income is just above the threshold. Exemption CREDITS, not base exemptions: IA 1040 Step 3 computes personal credits at $40 (enter 1 for statuses 1, 3, and 5; 2 for statuses 2 and 4), $20 per 65-or-older / blind condition, and $40 per dependent; the Step 3 total is a CREDIT against tax on line 8 — never a base reduction. exemptions ships empty; pass exemptions_count=0 and dependents_count=0, and pass the Step 3 counts as exemption_credit_counts (tax.exemption_credits, Phase K JK28). Low-income exemption (NOT modeled): filers whose Iowa taxable income plus specified add-backs is at or below $9,000 (single/MFS; $24,000 if 65+ on 12/31/25), or $13,500 (MFJ / HoH / QSS; $32,000 if 65+), owe no Iowa income tax (check the box the 2025 IA 1040 prints under the Step 5 heading, above line 5: "Check if using alternate tax (line 5), tax reduction calculation (line 12), or low-income exemption. See instructions." The Expanded Instructions' "Line 25" page still calls it "the box between Steps 4 and 5"); a dependent filer's threshold is $5,000; MFS also requires combined income of $13,500 or less. NEW for 2025: the federal Enhanced Deduction for Seniors is added back when testing this exemption. Cents vs whole dollars: the IA 1040 is captioned 'Enter Dollars and Cents' and computes tax to the cent; whole-dollar rounding is OPTIONAL (drop under 50 cents; 50-99 cents up — a .50 tie rounds UP, matching this op). No tax-table mandate: all filers apply the 3.8% rate (or the alternate-tax / tax-reduction worksheets). Not modeled — later lines: Iowa lump-sum tax (line 6), tuition and textbook credit (line 9), volunteer firefighter/EMS/reserve peace officer credit (line 10), the IA 126 nonresident/part-year credit, out-of-state tax credit, SCHOOL DISTRICT SURTAX and EMS surtax (line 19, in Step 5: "School district surtax or EMS surtax. Multiply line 18 by the percentage from list"; Step 6 is "Refundable Credits and Payments", lines 23-30), the 15%-of-federal Iowa EITC (line 25), and the child and dependent care / early childhood development credits (line 24).
